⚠️
High spike-to-average ratio. The peak day (27,723 VUs) is 21× the daily average during the low-activity months of Jan/Feb (683 VUs/day). Spikes of this magnitude may indicate ad-hoc or emergency tests rather than planned load tests. A scheduled, consistent load testing cadence produces more meaningful trend data and reduces surprise usage peaks.

Key Observations

✅
Mock Services adoption starting. Mock Services first appeared in April 2026 — a positive sign. Expanding mock usage decouples testing from live backend availability, enabling more parallel and earlier test runs.
✅
GUI Functional testing present. GUI Functional tests ran in Nov 2025 and Feb 2026, showing cross-capability use. Integrating GUI tests into CI/CD pipelines would make them continuous rather than periodic.
⚠️
Data-driven testing under-utilised. "Performance with TestData" was only used on 14 days and accounts for just 1.9% of total VUs. Parameterising tests with realistic datasets is one of the most impactful ways to improve test fidelity and catch data-related performance issues.
⚠️
Low-volume days. There are several days with ≤10 VUs (e.g., Jan 3, Jan 10, Jan 17, Feb 7, Dec 20, Dec 25). These suggest incomplete or abandoned test runs rather than meaningful load. Ensuring tests are properly instrumented and have realistic concurrency levels maximises the value of each run.
ℹ️
Weekend testing is minimal (6.7%). Most activity is weekday-focused, which is expected. However, for teams doing continuous delivery, scheduling lightweight regression smoke tests on weekends can catch issues before Monday releases.

Recommendations

📊
Enable API Monitoring
API Monitoring has 0 usage across the entire 6-month period. This feature provides continuous, always-on endpoint health checking without writing additional test scripts.
  • Create monitors from existing JMeter / Taurus scripts
  • Set SLA thresholds for response time and error rate
  • Configure alerts to Slack, PagerDuty, or email
  • Monitor key business-critical endpoints 24/7
High Priority
🗄️
Expand Data-Driven Testing
"Performance with TestData" accounts for only 1.9% of VUs. Data-driven tests use CSV or JSON datasets to simulate real-world user variance, uncovering issues that fixed-parameter tests miss.
  • Attach user data sets to existing JMeter tests
  • Parameterise authentication tokens, user IDs, and query strings
  • Use BlazeMeter's built-in TestData Manager for GDPR-safe synthetic data
High Priority
📅
Adopt a Regular Testing Cadence
Usage dropped 71% from Oct 2025 to Jan 2026. Irregular testing makes trend analysis unreliable and increases the risk of regressions going undetected.
  • Schedule weekly baseline tests from CI/CD (Jenkins, GitHub Actions)
  • Use BlazeMeter's built-in test scheduler for off-hours runs
  • Define a monthly "performance checkpoint" workload
  • Compare results against a stored baseline report
High Priority
🤖
Scale Mock Services Usage
Mock Services appeared for the first time in April 2026 — a great start. Expanding this reduces dependency on live environments and enables earlier testing.
  • Mock third-party APIs that are unreliable in test environments
  • Record and replay production traffic to create realistic mocks
  • Use mocks to run high-concurrency tests that would otherwise impact back-end systems
Medium Priority
🖥️
Integrate GUI Tests into CI/CD
GUI Functional and GUI Performance tests ran on only 8 distinct days — largely ad-hoc. Moving these into a pipeline delivers faster feedback.
  • Trigger GUI smoke tests on every pull request merge
  • Run GUI performance regression tests nightly
  • Use BZM's Selenium / Playwright integration
  • Combine with backend load tests on release branches
Medium Priority
🎯
Set Failure Criteria on All Tests
Many test executions show status "unset" — meaning no pass/fail criteria are defined. Without thresholds, a test that generates high error rates still shows green.
  • Define response time SLAs (e.g., P95 < 2 s)
  • Set maximum allowable error rate (e.g., < 1%)
  • Configure throughput floor thresholds
  • Enable "Stop test on violation" for critical pipelines
Medium Priority
📋
Reduce Low-Value Mini-Runs
Several days recorded ≤10 VUs, suggesting very short or misconfigured tests. These consume capacity without producing actionable data.
  • Set a minimum concurrency policy (e.g., ≥10 virtual users)
  • Add a ramp-up period to ensure steady-state metrics
  • Use the BlazeMeter test validation report before launching
Low Priority
🌐
Explore Multi-Region Load Tests
Current tests appear to run from single locations. Distributing load across multiple geographies provides a more realistic simulation of global user traffic.
  • Add US-East, EU-West, and APAC agents to existing tests
  • Test CDN effectiveness by comparing regional response times
  • Identify geo-specific latency or routing bottlenecks
Low Priority
